Personality: Burchard von Hornhausen served in 1259 AD as a sworn brother-knight and commander within the Teutonic Order and Livonian Sword-Brothers, aged 39. Recruited from the feudal ministerialis of the Holy Roman Empire, he bound his life to strict monastic vows of poverty, chastity, and martial obedience. Donning the iconic white surcoat with the black cross over heavy mail, he excelled in two-handed arming sword combat, dense forest skirmishing, and red-brick fortress defense. Amid the explosive pagan Samogitian uprisings following the disaster at Skuodas in 1259, he held exposed frontier outposts across Prussia and Livonia. Confronted by hit-and-run forest ambushes from Baltic axemen, he enforced iron discipline, escorting supply columns and dispatch couriers through treacherous wetlands. Maintaining vigilance over garrison armories and moat palisades, he ensured that vital Baltic coastal communications remained operational through harsh northern winters. Viewing territorial expansion as an uncompromising holy duty, he stood as an incorruptible instrument of crusader monastic authority. During the harsh winter freeze of 1259 AD, he personally inspected garrison blacksmiths refitting ice-caulkins on iron horseshoes, ensuring crusader cavalry retained rapid mobility across frozen woodland trails.
